izzyondroid:io.github.dorumrr.privacyfli.name: Privacy Flip
izzyondroid:io.github.dorumrr.privacyfli.summary: Manage your device privacy based on lock/unlock state
izzyondroid:io.github.dorumrr.privacyfli.description:
Privacy Flip automatically manages your device's privacy features based on screen lock/unlock state. When you lock your device, it can disable Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, mobile data, location services, NFC, and even camera/microphone sensors. When you unlock, it intelligently restores the features you want back on.
 Works with Sui, Root, Dhizuku or Shizuku - Choose your preferred privilege method! 
 Features: 
 Manage your device privacy based on lock/unlock state
 Four privilege methods: Sui, Root, Dhizuku or Shizuku (no root needed for Dhizuku or Shizuku)
 Automatic privilege detection (Sui > Root > Dhizuku > Shizuku)
 Configurable feature control (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Mobile Data, Location, NFC, Camera, Microphone, Airplane Mode, Battery Saver)
 Customizable timing delays (0-60 seconds granular, 2 minutes, or 5 minutes)
 Smart "only if unused/not connected" modes for WiFi, Bluetooth, Location, and Mobile Data while media plays
 App exemption system (skip privacy for specific foreground apps)
 Detects NFC being turned back on by a payment or wallet app, with opt-in auto-retry
 Optional Accessibility Service as an extra lock and unlock signal
 Advanced multi-tier Bluetooth connection detection
 Background service for persistent monitoring
 Quick Settings tile integration
 Home screen widget
 Privacy Features Controlled: 
 Wi-Fi - Disable/enable wireless connectivity
 Bluetooth - Control Bluetooth radio
 Mobile data - Manage cellular data connection
 Location services - Control GPS and location tracking
 NFC - Control NFC sensor
 Camera - Disable/enable camera sensor privacy (Android 12+)
 Microphone - Disable/enable microphone sensor privacy (Android 12+)
 Airplane Mode - Enable on lock (opt-in, disables all radios at once)
 Battery Saver - Enable on lock (opt-in, reduces background activity)
 Note: Camera and microphone ignore custom delays and trigger immediately, due to Android limitations. Microphone can skip this during a phone or VoIP call if enabled in settings; camera cannot detect active use, so it always triggers immediately
 Requirements: 
 Android 8.0+ (API level 26)
 Android 12+ (API level 31) for camera/microphone features
 Choose your privilege method: 
 Option 1: Shizuku (No root required!) * Shizuku app installed and running * ADB privileges via USB or wireless debugging * Perfect for non-rooted devices
 Option 2: Root Access (Recommended for rooted devices) * Root access via Magisk, SuperSU, or similar * Best performance with UID 0 privileges
 Option 3: Dhizuku (Device Owner method, 5 of 9 features) * Device set as Device Owner * No root required, no ADB after setup * Persistent privileges across reboots * Works for, each needing its own Android version: Camera and Microphone (Android 12+), Bluetooth (Android 9+), Location (Android 11+), NFC (Android 15+). Below Android 9 a Dhizuku setup can switch nothing at all. * Cannot do WiFi, Mobile Data, Airplane Mode or Battery Saver - Android gives a Device Owner no way to switch those. Use Root or Shizuku for them.
 Option 4: Sui (Best of both worlds) * Rooted device with Magisk * Sui Magisk module installed * Best user experience - automatic startup, no prompts
 Privacy & Security: 
 Zero telemetry - Nothing is sent to us or any third party
 Settings and the app's own lock state stay on your device, and in your own Android backup if you have one turned on - never sent anywhere else
 No network permissions - App cannot access internet
 Open source - https://github.com/dorumrr/privacyFlip

fdroid:ar.kevinroberts.nicotind.tv.name: NicotinD TV
fdroid:ar.kevinroberts.nicotind.tv.summary: Android TV player for your self-hosted NicotinD music server
fdroid:ar.kevinroberts.nicotind.tv.description:
NicotinD TV is the Android TV client for a self-hosted NicotinD music server. You run the server on your own machine; this app sits on the TV home row and streams your library to the living room. There is no NicotinD account, no cloud service, and nothing to sign up for — the only server the app talks to is the one whose address you give it.
You will need a NicotinD server before this app is useful. It runs in one Docker container on anything from a spare laptop to a NAS.
 Built for a remote, not a touchscreen 
This is a separate app from the phone client, not the same screens stretched out. It ships a ten-foot player, D-pad navigation throughout, and predictable Back behaviour, and it registers a channel on the Android TV home screen.
 What it does 
* Browses and streams your library — artists, albums, songs, genres, with cover art sized for across-the-room viewing.
* Metadata-driven radio that picks what comes next from BPM, musical key, genre and mood similarity rather than from a recommendation service.
* Synced lyrics with a karaoke-style vocal-mute option — the reason a lot of people want music on a TV in the first place.
* Plays in the background with system media controls, and accepts playback started from another NicotinD device.
* Multi-user, with per-user settings on one shared library.
 Privacy 
The app talks to your server and nothing else. No analytics, no advertising identifiers, no third-party SDKs. Your listening history lives in your own database.
 Connecting it 
TVs have no camera, so you connect the way TV apps always have: type your server's address, or enter the pairing code your server displays. This is not a limitation of this build — it is the only path on any TV.
 About this build 
This is the same APK the project publishes on its GitHub releases — one build, no F-Droid-only variant, and no proprietary library of any kind.
Installed from F-Droid, it updates through F-Droid, and its own in-app update button hides itself. That button exists for people who sideload, where it is the only way to update; the app asks Android who installed it and removes the control when a store did. This is why it declares the "install unknown apps" permission even though F-Droid will never use it here.
The TV app is a separate package from the phone app, so the two install side by side rather than replacing each other. If you sideloaded a TV APK before version 0.7, that older one used the phone package name and will not be upgraded by this — uninstall it by hand.
 Free software 
NicotinD is licensed under the AGPL-3.0. Source, issues and documentation: https://github.com/kevinch3/NicotinD

fdroid:biz.binarysolutions.stress.name: Perceived Stress Scale
fdroid:biz.binarysolutions.stress.summary: Are you stressed? Take the test to find out how stressed you are.
fdroid:biz.binarysolutions.stress.description:
The Perceived Stress Scale (PSS) is the most widely used psychological instrument for measuring the perception of stress. It is a measure of the degree to which situations in one's life are appraised as stressful. Items were designed to tap how unpredictable, uncontrollable, and overloaded respondents find their lives. The scale also includes a number of direct queries about current levels of experienced stress. The PSS was designed for use in community samples with at least a junior high school education. The items are easy to understand, and the response alternatives are simple to grasp. Moreover, the questions are of a general nature and hence are relatively free of content specific to any subpopulation group. The questions in the PSS ask about feelings and thoughts during the last month.
Evidence for Validity: Higher PSS scores were associated with (for example):
- failure to quit smoking
- failure among diabetics to control blood sugar levels
- greater vulnerability to stressful life-event-elicited depressive symptoms
- more colds
Because levels of appraised stress should be influenced by daily hassles, major events, and changes in coping resources, predictive validity of the PSS is expected to fall off rapidly after four to eight weeks.

fdroid:com.byarchitect.dejavu.description:
Dejavu is a web browser for Android built on Mozilla's Gecko engine, the same
engine Firefox uses. It keeps the same page rendering, add-ons and Mozilla account
sync, and replaces the way tabs are organised with something quieter.
Dejavu is an independent project. It is not made, endorsed or supported by
Mozilla. Firefox is a trademark of the Mozilla Foundation in the U.S. and other
countries.
Instead of one long list of tabs, Dejavu gives you:
* Workspaces - separate sets of tabs for separate parts of your life, each with
 its own colour theme and icon.
* Containers - keep sites signed in to different accounts apart, per workspace.
* Pinned tabs and essentials - the pages you always want open, always in reach.
* Folders - group tabs inside a workspace and collapse them out of the way.
* Split view - two pages side by side.
* A single bottom bar with every action, and an address field that stays out of
 the way at the top.
Sync: Dejavu signs in with your Mozilla account and syncs workspaces, pinned
tabs, essentials, folders and containers with Zen Browser on the desktop. Or it
follows Firefox: each of your computers and phones with Firefox gets its own
workspace, with its pinned tabs and tab groups, and opening or closing a tab
there does the same in Firefox. Bookmarks, history and passwords sync too.
Private by default: Dejavu sends no telemetry or crash reports, shows no
sponsored content, and search suggestions are off from the first launch.
Dejavu is free software under the Mozilla Public License 2.0. Its source code is
at https://github.com/by-architect/Dejavu

• Show figures three ways, as Fava does: Units, At cost, or Market value.
• Add entries and other Beancount directives with a form that shows the exact text before it is written.
• Edit the files themselves, with every save re-read by Beancount before it is called saved, and an Undo for the last change.
• Scan receipts and statements into PDFs and file them under an account.
• Open Fava's Reports inside the app.
• Mirror a project to a folder you choose, and back it up with an optional passphrase.
• Use Beancount plugins and Fava extensions, and run your own Python scripts.
• Home-screen widgets for balances and net worth.
 Your data stays yours 
• No telemetry, analytics, crash uploads or ads.
• Local mode makes no network requests.
• If you turn on Share on Wi-Fi, other devices can reach your Reports only while it is on, only on a private network, and only after signing in.
• Nothing is sold, and there is nothing to subscribe to.
 Two editions 
The Expert edition adds plugins and packages that include native code, fetched only when you ask. The Play edition does without them. Both are free.
Beanbook is an independent project. It is built on Beancount and Fava and is not affiliated with or endorsed by them. It comes with no warranty, as its GPL-2.0 licence states: keep backups of your ledger.

flathub:com.github.debauchee.barrier.description:
What is it?
 Barrier is software that mimics the functionality of a KVM switch, which historically would allow you to use a single keyboard and mouse to control multiple computers by physically turning a dial on the box to switch the machine you're controlling at any given moment. Barrier does this in software, allowing you to tell it which machine to control by moving your mouse to the edge of the screen, or by using a keypress to switch focus to a different system.
 Barrier was forked from Symless's Synergy 1.9 codebase. Synergy was a commercialized reimplementation of the original CosmoSynergy written by Chris Schoeneman.
 What's different?
 Whereas Synergy has moved beyond its goals from the 1.x era, Barrier aims to maintain that simplicity. Barrier will let you use your keyboard and mouse from machine A to control machine B (or more). It's that simple.
 Project goals
 Hassle-free reliability. We are users, too. Barrier was created so that we could solve the issues we had with synergy and then share these fixes with other users.
 Compatibility. We use more than one operating system and you probably do, too. Windows, OSX, Linux, FreeBSD... Barrier should "just work". We will also have our eye on Wayland when the time comes.
 Communication. Everything we do is in the open. Our issue tracker will let you see if others are having the same problem you're having and will allow you to add additional information. You will also be able to see when progress is made and how the issue gets resolved.

What is Add to Buyee?
It is a PC-only browser extension developed by Buyee, a Japanese proxy buying service.
How is it useful?
Add to Buyee allows you to shop at over 150 popular Japanese e-commerce sites such as Amazon JP, Mercari, and Animate.
You can easily buy products from multiple sites by simply adding them to your Add to Buyee shopping cart!
Here is a quick guide on how to use Add to Buyee.
Shopping Flow
①Add the Add to Buyee tool from this page
②Go to the page of the product you want on the Japanese shopping site
③Click the Add to Buyee button
④Select your desired color, size, etc., and click ""Add to Cart""
⑤Click the ""Cart"" button
⑥After confirming the items in your Buyee cart, click ""Proceed to order""
※You must be logged in and registered as a Buyee member to use this service.
Shipping Flow
①When your package arrives at the warehouse, specify the destination and shipping method (pay the shipping fee)
②Shipping your package
For a list of sites and detailed instructions on how to use them, click here:
 https://buyee.jp/addtobuyee/index 
Now, let's start shopping on Japanese e-commerce sites using Add to Buyee!
■Service Introduction
Buyee is a service that helps customers purchase products from Japanese and US e-commerce sites and delivers them worldwide.
Why use Buyee?
①Extensive track record
Over 4.5 million members in 110 countries/regions worldwide.
②Partnership with Japanese e-commerce sites
We work with popular Japanese shopping websites such as JDirectItems Auction, Rakuten, Mercari, etc., so you can shop with confidence.
③Safe multilingual support
Customer support is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year in 17 languages, so you can shop online confidently even if you do not understand Japanese.
Buyee is here to support you and ensure a great shopping experience!

apple-macos:6670346172.description:
Fly freely to any place in the world.
With 3D satellite maps, you can glide smoothly above cities, mountains, oceans, and landmarks from an aerial view.
When you want to create stunning aerial videos
When you're planning a trip
When you want to explore places you haven't visited yet
Skymera lets you shape the scene you want with drone-like, natural camera movement.
◆ See the world from above, more vividly
Skymera brings landscapes and details to life with 3D maps and satellite views.
Turn what you're seeing on screen into an aerial map video, just as it is - cities, mountains, oceans, and landmarks.
◆ Create your own flight route
Once you have a scene in mind, just add keyframes.
Set up to 20 points per route and adjust direction, angle, and altitude at each point to create the map animation you want.
From orbiting around buildings to zooming down from the sky, bring your imagined scene to life.
◆ Map styles that match your video mood
Choose a map style that fits your video's vibe.
Clean road map
Hybrid map with satellite imagery and road names
Satellite-only map
Switching styles can make the same route feel completely different.
◆ From preview to high-quality recording
Preview and save your finished route right away.
Preview your flight path, then record it as a video. Find and share your recordings from the app’s saved videos list.
Share your saved videos on social media.
Skymera's 3D map videos work great for travel memories and also for promos, Reels, Shorts, and more.
◆ Popular routes from creators worldwide
Creators around the world keep sharing routes crafted from their own perspectives.
If you're not sure where to start, browse popular routes for ideas.
When you share your route, it can inspire someone else's travel plans or content.
Follow another route to discover new scenes, then recreate it in your own style.
Ready to go?
Start your first flight now.
